full_text_sections.full_text: Scientific Reports | (2026) 16:31685 1 www.nature.com/scientificreports | https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-72549-0 OPEN 1Department of Mathematics, Faculty of Science, Umm Al-Qura University, 21955 Makkah, Saudi Arabia. 2Department of Mathematics and Computer Science, Faculty of Science, Beni-Suef University, 26511 Beni-Suef, Egypt. email: Bahaa_gm@yahoo.com Fractional optimal control of hantavirus transmission between rodents and humans A. H. Qamlo1 & G. M. Bahaa 2 This paper studies a fractional optimal control problem for a hantavirus transmission model involving interactions between rodent reservoirs and human populations. The model is formulated through a modified SIR–SIR structure, where both humans and rodents are divided into susceptible, infected, and recovered classes. The classical integer-order model is extended by using the Caputo fractional derivative, which captures memory and hereditary effects in the disease dynamics. Three time- dependent control variables are introduced: rodent culling, environmental sanitation, and treatment of infected humans. Positivity, boundedness, existence, and uniqueness of solutions are established to guarantee the biological and mathematical validity of the model. An optimal control problem is then formulated to minimize infected humans, infected rodents, and the costs of intervention. Necessary optimality conditions are derived using Pontryagin’s maximum principle for fractional systems. The adjoint equations, transversality conditions, and explicit characterization of the optimal controls are obtained. A numerical scheme based on the fractional Adams–Bashforth–Moulton predictor–corrector method combined with the forward–backward sweep algorithm is implemented. Several numerical scenarios are investigated, including no control, single-control strategies, and combined optimal controls. The simulations show that the combined strategy gives the strongest reduction in both infected humans and infected rodents. The results illustrate how memory-dependent dynamics can alter the predicted transmission trajectories and optimal intervention profiles. However, empirical calibration and validation using compatible human and rodent surveillance data are required before the model can be used for outbreak-specific prediction. The disease represents an important global public health challenge because of its high mortality rates, rapid respiratory complications, and increasing geographical spread4–6. Several strains of hantaviruses have been identified worldwide, including strains responsible for hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome7–9. Human infection generally occurs through inhalation of aerosolized particles from infected rodents, although evidence of human-to- human transmission has also been reported in specific outbreaks10 (Fig. 1). Rodents are considered the principal reservoirs of hantaviruses12,13. Long-term epidemiological studies confirmed that environmental conditions, climate fluctuations, rodent migration, and habitat changes play significant roles in the persistence and transmission of hantavirus infection14–18. In Asia and South America, several investigations revealed increasing prevalence rates associated with ecological changes and urbanization5,9,19. In Indonesia, hantavirus infections have attracted increasing scientific interest due to the existence of infected rodent reservoirs in several provinces20–22. Mathematical modeling has become an essential tool for understanding the spread and control of infectious diseases23–26. Classical epidemic models based on ordinary differential equations have been successfully applied to many zoonotic diseases27,28. Several mathematical models for hantavirus transmission have been developed in the literature. Abramson and Kenkre studied spatial and spatiotemporal patterns in hantavirus spread14,15. Allen et al. proposed deterministic and ecological models describing rodent-host interactions and environmental variability29–31. Additional modeling investigations involving ecological risk mapping, stochastic fluctuations, and environmental effects were developed in33–35. Although classical integer-order models provide useful qualitative insights, they often fail to capture memory and hereditary effects observed in biological systems. Many infectious diseases exhibit nonlocal temporal dynamics in which the future state depends not only on the present state but also on the history of the system. Fractional calculus provides a powerful mathematical framework for incorporating these memory effects into epidemiological models36–38. Fractional-order epidemic models have shown improved accuracy in describing long-memory biological processes and nonlinear transmission dynamics39. Biological justification for the Caputo derivative The use of the Caputo fractional derivative is motivated by biological and epidemiological processes that depend on accumulated history rather than only on the current state. Hantavirus risk is influenced by prior rodent abundance, repeated or prolonged contact with contaminated excreta, persistence of infectious material in the environment, delayed effects of habitat and climate variation, and time-distributed host recovery and immune responses. These mechanisms introduce temporal dependence that may not be represented adequately by a local first-order derivative. The Caputo operator describes such effects through a power-law memory kernel, so recent and earlier epidemic states contribute with different weights to the present rate of change. It is also suitable for population models because it permits conventional initial conditions expressed directly through the initial compartment sizes. The fractional order inline-eq-IEq1 is therefore interpreted as a phenomenological memory parameter. Its epidemiological relevance should be assessed through sensitivity analysis, parameter estimation, and comparison with observed data. Recently, fractional optimal control theory has received considerable attention in mathematical biology and engineering40. The combination of fractional dynamics and optimal control allows the construction of realistic control strategies that account for memory-dependent disease behavior while minimizing intervention costs. Several important developments in fractional optimal control systems were established in41–43. Applications involving epidemic systems, cancer dynamics, and quantum systems, dark mater in cosmological models demonstrated the efficiency of fractional optimal control formulations44–48. Despite the large number of studies devoted to hantavirus transmission dynamics, very few works considered fractional-order optimal control formulations for hantavirus systems. Most existing models are formulated using classical differential equations without incorporating memory effects or optimal intervention strategies. Moreover, the combined effects of rodent reduction, environmental sanitation, and treatment controls within a fractional-order framework remain insufficiently investigated. papers.title_zh: 分数阶最优控制 汉坦病毒 在啮齿动物与人类之间的传播

analysis_zh.background: 本研究针对 汉坦病毒 在啮齿动物与人类之间的传播进行探讨,该人畜共患病致死率高且地理分布正在扩大。
analysis_zh.methods: 构建了含 Caputo 导数的分数阶 SIR–SIR 模型,纳入啮齿动物扑杀、环境卫生和人类治疗作为时变控制;证明了模型的存在性、唯一性和正性,并运用 Pontryagin 最大原理推导最优性条件;数值模拟采用分数阶 Adams–Bashforth–Moulton 预测-校正方案结合前向-后向扫描。
analysis_zh.results: 模拟结果表明,综合控制策略能够最大程度降低人类和啮齿动物的感染数;记忆效应改变了传播轨迹和最优干预方案;但模型缺乏实证校准。
analysis_zh.contribution: 本研究展示了分数动力学如何提升 汉坦病毒 建模,并为最优干预设计提供依据,强调了数据驱动验证的必要性。
analysis_zh.limitations: 该模型尚未使用监测数据进行实证校准或验证,限制了其即时的预测效用。

papers.title: Current State of Diagnostics of Hemorrhagic Fevers Caused by Viruses of the Genera Orthonairovirus, Phlebovirus, Orthohantavirus and Orthoflavivirus, Using the LAMP Method
papers.abstract: The work is an overview of the data on application of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) for the diagnosis of viral hemorrhagic fevers caused by pathogens belonging to the second pathogenicity group. The first part of the review provides a brief characterization of the main viral agents of hemorrhagic fevers from the families Nairoviridae, Phenuiviridae, Hantaviridae, and Flaviviridae. Special attention is given to the epidemiological significance of these pathogens and the challenges associated with their timely laboratory identification. The aim of the study was to analyze and systematize the data available in the literature sources on the use of LAMP as an alternative to polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for diagnosing hemorrhagic fevers caused by these agents. The review considers the principal methods for registering LAMP results, including the turbidimetric method, immunochromatographic assays, the use of fluorescent dyes, metal-based indicators and pH-sensitive dyes. A comparative analysis of the analytical characteristics of existing LAMP reagent kits for each of the described agents is also presented. It is noted that there are currently no registered and widely available commercial LAMP reagent kits for detecting the genetic markers of these viruses. This underscores the need for further research, since the implementation of rapid and reliable diagnostic methods suitable for field use is a prerequisite for effective epidemic control measures. Therefore, the development of appropriate reagent kits based on the LAMP method represents a promising objective.

The aim of the study was to analyze and systematize the data available in the literature sources on the use of LAMP as an alternative to polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for diagnosing hemorrhagic fevers caused by these agents. The review considers the principal methods for registering LAMP results, including the turbidimetric method, immunochromatographic assays, the use of fluorescent dyes, metal-based indicators and pH-sensitive dyes. A comparative analysis of the analytical characteristics of existing LAMP reagent kits for each of the described agents is also presented. It is noted that there are currently no registered and widely available commercial LAMP reagent kits for detecting the genetic markers of these viruses. This underscores the need for further research, since the implementation of rapid and reliable diagnostic methods suitable for field use is a prerequisite for effective epidemic control measures. Therefore, the development of appropriate reagent kits based on the LAMP method represents a promising objective.

Такие серьезные заболевания часто вызывают вирусы I и II группы патогенности, со­ гласно российской классификации патогенных для человека микроорганизмов. К вирусам II группы патогенности, вызывающим ВГЛ у людей, относят­ ся некоторые представители родов Orthonairovirus (сем. Nairoviridae), Phlebovirus (сем. Phenuiviridae), Orthohantavirus (сем. Hantaviridae) и Orthoflavivirus (сем. Flaviviridae) (табл. 1). Эти вирусы, способные вызывать вспышки ВГЛ с высокой летальностью, представляют большой ин­ терес для здравоохранения. В роде Orthonairovirus CCHFV способен вы­ зывать Крымскую-Конго геморрагическую ли­ хорадку, переносимую клещами рода Hyalomma. Зарегистрированы случаи заболевания данной ли­ хорадкой в Азии, Юго-Западной и Юго-Восточной Европе и Африке [1]. Инфекция у человека может протекать как в легкой форме, без специфических клинических симптомов, так и в тяжелой форме, до­ стигая уровня летальности 40 % [2]. Геном CCHFV состоит из трех сегментов РНК с отрицательной по­ лярностью: S (1,7 кб), M (5,4 кб) и L (12,1 кб). Вирус обладает большим генетическим разнообразием и демонстрирует высокую изменчивость во всех трех сегментах. Так, разница в нуклеотидной последо­ вательности для S-сегмента составляет 20 %, для M – 31 %, для L – 22 % [3, 4]. В аминокислотной последовательности S- и L-сегменты также более консервативны (95 %), чем M-сегмент (до 75 %) [4]. Выделяется 7 генетических линий, основанных на S-сегменте: Африка 1–3, Азия 1, 2 и Европа 1, 2. RVFV из рода Phlebovirus является возбудите­ лем одноименного зоонозного заболевания, пере­ носимого комарами родов Aedes, Culex, Anopheles, Eretmapoites, Mansonia. Лихорадка долины Рифт была зарегистрирована в большинстве африканских стран, Саудовской Аравии и Йемене. Заболевание может протекать в тяжелой форме с ретинитом, ге­ патитом и энцефалитом, у 1 % пациентов развива­ ется геморрагическая лихорадка, уровень летально­ сти достигает 50 % [5, 6]. Геном вируса состоит из двух сегментов РНК с отрицательной полярностью M (3,9 кб) и L (6,4 кб) и одного сегмента амбисенс­ ной РНК – S (1,7 кб) [7]. Геном RVFV достаточно консервативен, лишь М-сегмент имеет небольшие различия в нуклеотидной (5 %) и аминокислотной (2 %) последовательности [8]. Хантавирусы (род Orthohantavirus) способны вызывать у человека геморрагическую лихорадку с почечным синдромом (ГЛПС) и хантавирусный пульмональный синдром (ХПС), передаваемые грызунами. Случаи заболевания ГЛПС, вызванные пре­имущественно вирусом Хантаан (HTNV), за­ регистрированы в Европе, России и Азии [9]. В за­ висимости от возбудителя уровень летальности до­ стигает 15 %. Геном представлен тремя сегментами РНК отрицательной полярности: S (1,0–3,0 кб), M (3,4–4,8 кб) и L (5,3–6,8 кб) [11]. Последовательность L-сегмента наиболее консерва­ тивна, а M-сегмента – наименее [12]. В роде Orthoflavivirus представителями II груп­ пы патогенности, вызывающими ВГЛ у людей, являются: вирус болезни леса Кьясанур (KFDV), вирус желтой лихорадки (YFV), вирус омской ге­ моррагической лихорадки (OHFV) и вирус денге со всеми серотипами (DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3, DENV-4). Геном ортофлавивирусов несегментиро­ ванный, пред­ставляет собой РНК положительной полярности длиной 9,2–11 кб. Одна открытая рамка считывания коди­рует полипротеин, который в ходе процессинга расщепляется протеазами на три струк­ турных (C, prM и E) и семь неструктурных белков (NS1, NS2A, NS2B, NS3, NS4A, NS4B и NS5) [13]. KFDV циркулирует преимущественно в Индии, пе­ реносчиком вируса являются клещи Haemaphysalis spinigera. При заболевании в 10–20 % случаев раз­ виваются невро­логические осложнения, а уровень летальности составляет 3–5 % [14]. YFV переносит­ ся комарами рода Aedes в субтропических регионах Африки и Haema­gogus в Южной Америке, достигая при тяжелом течении высокого уровня летальности – 40–60 % и 1–5 % – для всех инфицированных [15]. OHFV эндемичен в Западной Сибири и переносит­ ся клещами родов Dermacentor и Ixodes. Уровень смертности от вирусной инфекции составляет около 0,5–3 % [16]. Лихорадка денге эндемична в тропи­ ческих и субтропических регионах Африки, Юго- Восточной Азии, Западной части Тихого океана и Америки, а также встречается в некоторых регио­ нах Европы. В основном DENV передается кома­ рами рода Aedes, а уровень смертности составляет 2–5 % [17]. DENV состоит из четырех различных серотипов (DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3, DENV-4), имеющих 65–70 % идентичности аминокислотных последовательностей [18]. В связи с тем, что разные возбудители на ранней стадии вызывают схожие лихорадочные симптомы, необходима разработка быстрой и надежной диффе­ ренциальной диагностики ВГЛ. Лабораторная диа­ гностика ВГЛ в основном основана на иммунохими­ ческих, серологических и молекулярно-генетических методах. Самыми распространенными молекулярно- генетическими методами на ранней стадии развития инфекции являются ПЦР и ПЦР с обратной транс­ крипцией (ОТ-ПЦР), отличающиеся высокой чув­ ствительностью и специфичностью. Однако методы изотермической амплификации превосходят ПЦР и ОТ-ПЦР в скорости получения результата (30– 40 мин) [19–22]. Для проведения реакции не требует­ ся дорогостоящее и сложное термоцик­лирующее обо­ рудование. Амплификация проходит при постоянной температуре, что позволяет использовать простые и доступные приборы, например термостат или водя­ ную баню. Сочетание высокой скорости и простоты оборудования делает ее незаменимым инструментом для проведения молекулярно-диагностических ис­ следований непосредственно на месте оказания по­ мощи (point-of-care testing), в полевых условиях и в отдаленных районах. Таким образом, методы изотермической ампли­ фикации представляют значительный интерес для разработки диагностических наборов реагентов. Цель работы – анализ и систематизация имею­ щихся данных о диагностике методом LAMP гемор­ рагических лихорадок, вызываемых возбудителями, которые относятся к II группе патогенности. На конец 2025 г. имеются сведения о 42 диагно­ стических наборах реагентов, 10 из которых – муль­ типлексные, основанные на методе LAMP для обна­ ружения вирусов II группы патогенности, вызываю­ щих ВГЛ у людей (табл. 2). Диагностика CCHFV. Во всех исследованиях, посвященных разработке наборов реагентов для вы­ явления РНК CCHFV методом LAMP, олигонуклео­ тидные праймеры были подобраны на наиболее кон­ сервативный сегмент S. В исследовании J.S. Kumar et al. [25] набор реагентов был разработан с учетом 50 различных геномов CCHFV и успешно проте­ стирован на образцах, взятых у людей и клещей. Перекрестных реакций с геномами вирусов DENV, KFDV, YFV, японского энцефалита, Западного Нила, энцефалита Сент-Луис и Чикунгунья не наблюда­ лось. Результаты реакции детектировали при помо­ щи турбидиметра в режиме реального времени, из­ меряя оптическую плотность реакционной смеси, и визуально, используя интеркалирующий краси­ тель SYBR Green I. В основе турбидиметрического метода лежит увеличение мутности вследствие на­ копления осадка пирофосфата магния (Mg2P2O7), которое прямо пропорционально количеству синте­ зированной ДНК. В случае положительной реакции при детекции красителем SYBR Green I смесь из­ меняет оранжевый цвет на зеленый, а при свечении ультрафиолетом наблюдается зеленая флуоресцен­ ция. В других работах также популярными являются методы детекции с использованием красителя SYBR Green [23], EvaGreen в режиме реального времени [22, 24] и электрофорез в агарозном геле [23, 24, 26]. В результате разработанный набор реагентов мето­ дом LAMP [25] показал одинаковый предел чувстви­ тельности (104 копий/мл) с ОТ-ПЦР в режиме реаль­ ного времени. В исследовании H.A.M. Osman et al. [23] был раз­ работан набор реагентов на основе штамма CCHFV генетической линии Африка 3. Чуб1 Современное состояние диагностики геморрагических лихорадок, вызываемых вирусами родов Orthonairovirus, Phlebovirus, Orthohantavirus и Orthoflavivirus методом LAMP 1Государственный научный центр вирусологии и биотехнологии «Вектор», р.п. Кольцово, Российская Федерация; 2Новосибирский национальный исследовательский государственный университет, Новосибирск, Российская Федерация Представлен обзор данных о применении метода петлевой изотермической амплификации (loop mediated isothermal amplification, LAMP) для диагностики вирусных геморрагических лихорадок, вызываемых возбудите­ лями, относящимися к II группе патогенности. Дана краткая характеристика основных вирусных возбудителей геморрагических лихорадок из семейств Nairoviridae, Phenuiviridae, Hantaviridae и Flaviviridae. Особое внимание уделено эпидемиологической значимости данных патогенов и сложности их своевременной лабораторной иден­ тификации. Основная цель работы заключалась в анализе и систематизации имеющихся в литературе данных об использовании метода LAMP как альтернативы ПЦР для диагностики геморрагических лихорадок, вызываемых данными возбудителями. Рассмотрены основные методы детекции результатов LAMP, включая турбидиметри­ ческий метод, иммунохроматографический анализ, использование флуоресцентных красителей, металлоинди­ каторов и pH-чувствительных красителей. Проведен сравнительный анализ аналитических характеристик раз­ работанных наборов реагентов для LAMP-диагностики каждого из рассматриваемых возбудителей. Отмечается, что в настоящее время не существует зарегистрированных и широкодоступных коммерческих LAMP-наборов реагентов для выявления генетических маркеров данных вирусов. Это актуализирует необходимость дальнейших исследований, так как внедрение быстрых и надежных методов диагностики, пригодных для использования в полевых условиях, является необходимым условием эффективных противоэпидемических мероприятий. Таким образом, разработка соответствующих наборов реагентов на основе метода LAMP представляет собой перспек­ тивную задачу. Ключевые слова: геморрагическая лихорадка, изотермическая амплификация, LAMP, диагностика. Корреспондирующий автор: Беличенко Ксения Руслановна, e-mail: ksenbelichen@gmail.com. Для цитирования: Беличенко К.Р., Материкина Е.И., Чуб Е.В. Современное состояние диагностики геморрагических лихорадок, вызываемых вирусами родов Orthonairovirus, Phlebovirus, Orthohantavirus и Orthoflavivirus методом LAMP. Проблемы особо опасных инфекций. 2026; 3:6–15. DOI: 10.21055/0370-1069- 2026-3-6-15 Поступила 08.04.2026. Отправлена на доработку 15.05.2026. Принята к публикации 24.05.2026. K.R. Belichenko1,2, E.I. Materikina1, E.V. Chub1 Current State of Diagnostics of Hemorrhagic Fevers Caused by Viruses of the Genera Orthonairovirus, Phlebovirus, Orthohantavirus and Orthoflavivirus, Using the LAMP Method 1State Scientific Center of Virology and Biotechnology “Vector”, Kol’tsovo, Russian Federation; 2Novosibirsk National Research State University, Novosibirsk, Russian Federation Abstract. The work is an overview of the data on application of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) for the diagnosis of viral hemorrhagic fevers caused by pathogens belonging to the second pathogenicity group. The first part of the review provides a brief characterization of the main viral agents of hemorrhagic fevers from the families Nairoviridae, Phenuiviridae, Hantaviridae, and Flaviviridae. Special attention is given to the epidemiological significance of these pathogens and the challenges associated with their timely laboratory identification. The aim of the study was to analyze and systematize the data available in the literature sources on the use of LAMP as an alternative to polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for diagnosing hemorrhagic fevers caused by these agents. The review considers the principal methods for registering LAMP results, including the turbidimetric method, immunochromatographic as­ says, the use of fluorescent dyes, metal-based indicators and pH-sensitive dyes. A comparative analysis of the analytical characteristics of existing LAMP reagent kits for each of the described agents is also presented. It is noted that there are currently no registered and widely available commercial LAMP reagent kits for detecting the genetic markers of these viruses. This underscores the need for further research, since the implementation of rapid and reliable diagnostic methods suitable for field use is a prerequisite for effective epidemic control measures. Therefore, the development of appropriate reagent kits based on the LAMP method represents a promising objective. Key words: hemorrhagic fever, isothermal amplification, LAMP, diagnostics. Conflict of interest: The authors declare no conflict of interest. 7 Problemy Osobo Opasnykh Infektsii [Problems of Particularly Dangerous Infections]. 2026; 3 Reviews Вирусные геморрагические лихорадки (ВГЛ) характеризуются нарушением регуляции крове­ носных сосудов, что может приводить к дисфунк­ ции органов. Такие серьезные заболевания часто вызывают вирусы I и II группы патогенности, со­ гласно российской классификации патогенных для человека микроорганизмов. К вирусам II группы патогенности, вызывающим ВГЛ у людей, относят­ ся некоторые представители родов Orthonairovirus (сем. Nairoviridae), Phlebovirus (сем. Phenuiviridae), Orthohantavirus (сем. Hantaviridae) и Orthoflavivirus (сем. Flaviviridae) (табл. 1). Эти вирусы, способные вызывать вспышки ВГЛ с высокой летальностью, представляют большой ин­ терес для здравоохранения. В роде Orthonairovirus CCHFV способен вы­ зывать Крымскую-Конго геморрагическую ли­ хорадку, переносимую клещами рода Hyalomma. Зарегистрированы случаи заболевания данной ли­ хорадкой в Азии, Юго-Западной и Юго-Восточной Европе и Африке [1]. Инфекция у человека может протекать как в легкой форме, без специфических клинических симптомов, так и в тяжелой форме, до­ стигая уровня летальности 40 % [2]. Геном CCHFV состоит из трех сегментов РНК с отрицательной по­ лярностью: S (1,7 кб), M (5,4 кб) и L (12,1 кб). Вирус обладает большим генетическим разнообразием и демонстрирует высокую изменчивость во всех трех сегментах. Так, разница в нуклеотидной последо­ вательности для S-сегмента составляет 20 %, для M – 31 %, для L – 22 % [3, 4]. В аминокислотной последовательности S- и L-сегменты также более консервативны (95 %), чем M-сегмент (до 75 %) [4]. Выделяется 7 генетических линий, основанных на S-сегменте: Африка 1–3, Азия 1, 2 и Европа 1, 2. RVFV из рода Phlebovirus является возбудите­ лем одноименного зоонозного заболевания, пере­ носимого комарами родов Aedes, Culex, Anopheles, Eretmapoites, Mansonia. Лихорадка долины Рифт была зарегистрирована в большинстве африканских стран, Саудовской Аравии и Йемене. Заболевание может протекать в тяжелой форме с ретинитом, ге­ патитом и энцефалитом, у 1 % пациентов развива­ ется геморрагическая лихорадка, уровень летально­ сти достигает 50 % [5, 6]. Геном вируса состоит из двух сегментов РНК с отрицательной полярностью M (3,9 кб) и L (6,4 кб) и одного сегмента амбисенс­ ной РНК – S (1,7 кб) [7]. Геном RVFV достаточно консервативен, лишь М-сегмент имеет небольшие различия в нуклеотидной (5 %) и аминокислотной (2 %) последовательности [8]. Хантавирусы (род Orthohantavirus) способны вызывать у человека геморрагическую лихорадку с почечным синдромом (ГЛПС) и хантавирусный пульмональный синдром (ХПС), передаваемые грызунами. Случаи заболевания ГЛПС, вызванные пре­имущественно вирусом Хантаан (HTNV), за­ регистрированы в Европе, России и Азии [9]. В за­ висимости от возбудителя уровень летальности до­ стигает 15 %. papers.title: Driven magnetic 3D DNA walker coupled with CHA based on light-activatable hairpin: A dual-amplification strategy for ultrasensitive hantavirus RNA sensing.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Orthohantavirus dabieshanense (DBSV) is a newly emerging hantavirus and poses a potential threat to human health. Current detection methods based on polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assays for other hantaviruses such as Hantaan virus (HTNV) and Seoul virus (SEOV) may carry the risk of false negatives. This study aims to address the technical bottlenecks of low accuracy and insufficient sensitivity in current detection of DBSV. RESULTS: We developed a signal amplification strategy mediated by a photoactivated magnetic 3D DNA walker, which enables light-controllable fluorescence detection. Specifically, this fluorescence sensing platform introduces the catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) technique for dual signal amplification. This system requires dual activation by UV irradiation and target RNA. Then, exonuclease III (Exo III) provides propulsion for the walking process to release a specific trigger strand, subsequently activating the CHA cycle and producing a fluorescent signal. Experimental results confirm that the system displays excellent selectivity and anti-interference ability, successfully distinguishing target sequences with single-base mismatch (SBM), double-base mismatch (DBM), and triple-base mismatch (TBM). Furthermore, the platform achieves a DBSV-RNA detection limit (LOD) of 30 fM with a linear range spanning 10-1-106 pM. The applicability of the method has been rigorously validated using human serum specimens. SIGNIFICANCE: This study provides a novel strategy for the application of spatiotemporally controllable DNA walkers in RNA detection, demonstrating considerable potential for early viral diagnosis and field monitoring.

analysis.background: Orthohantavirus dabieshanense (DBSV) is a newly emerging hantavirus and poses a potential threat to human health (A1).
analysis.methods: A fluorescence sensing platform was built using a photo‑activated magnetic 3D DNA walker combined with catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA); activation requires UV irradiation and target RNA, and exonuclease III drives the walking process to release a trigger strand that initiates CHA (A4‑A7). The system was evaluated with human serum specimens (A10).
analysis.results: The platform displayed excellent selectivity, distinguishing single‑, double‑ and triple‑base mismatches (A8), achieved a detection limit of 30 fM for DBSV RNA with a linear range of 10⁻¹‑10⁶ pM (A9), and performed successfully in serum samples (A10).
analysis.contribution: The study introduces a novel, spatiotemporally controllable DNA‑walker strategy for ultrasensitive RNA detection, indicating considerable potential for early viral diagnosis and field monitoring (A11).
analysis.limitations: Only an abstract is provided; detailed experimental design, sample size, statistical analysis, and field validation are not reported (abstract_only).

analysis.summary_en: Background: Orthohantavirus dabieshanense (DBSV) is a newly emerging hantavirus threatening human health. Methods: The authors created a fluorescence platform using a photo‑activated magnetic 3D DNA walker coupled with catalytic hairpin assembly, requiring UV light and target RNA, with exonuclease III‑driven walking; it was tested on human serum. papers.title: Pathogens of Zoonotic Viral Infections, Circulating in Populations of Small Mammals: an Overview of the Current State
papers.abstract: Small mammals (rodents, insectivores, and bats) are the main reservoirs for a wide range of zoonotic viruses. These include the agents of vector-borne infections transmitted via bites of blood-sucking arthropods (ixodid ticks, mosquitoes, sand flies) and non-vector-borne infections (orthohantaviruses and others). Natural foci of viral infections, the reservoir of which are small mammals, are of primary epidemiological significance in the Russian Federation: hundreds of cases are recorded annually, many of which are severe. The aim of this review was to summarize current data on the circulation of viral zoonotic pathogens in small mammal populations in natural foci in the Russian Federation and worldwide, as well as to identify key issues in epizootiological surveillance and the study of reservoir relationships between hosts, pathogens, and vectors. It has been shown that among the zoonotic viruses circulating with the participation of rodents and insectivores, along with the most significant and widespread, returning (re-emerging) pathogens that pose a serious global and regional threat are also of great epidemiological importance. These are representatives of the Flaviviridae family (tick-borne encephalitis virus, Omsk hemorrhagic fever virus, Kyasanur forest disease virus), Bunyaviridae (orthohantaviruses, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus, and others), and Coronaviridae families. It was noted that small mammals acted not only as reservoir hosts for viruses but also as feeders, ensuring the maintenance of populations of vectors (ixodid and argasid ticks, mosquitoes and midges), thereby creating stable parasitic systems. The issue of zoonotic viruses circulating among small mammals remains urgent for both the Russian Federation and the global community. Analysis of global trends indicates that infectious diseases of animals are expanding their range, thereat many of them with zoonotic potential. The key drivers of this process are climate change, expansion of international trade and transformation of ecosystems, requiring improved epidemiological monitoring and an interdisciplinary approach to risk assessment.

analysis.background: Small mammals serve as primary reservoirs for zoonotic viruses, posing significant epidemiological risks in the Russian Federation and globally, with hundreds of severe cases recorded annually.
analysis.methods: This review summarizes current data on viral zoonotic pathogen circulation in small mammal populations within natural foci in the Russian Federation and worldwide, focusing on epizootiological surveillance and host-pathogen-vector relationships.
analysis.results: The review identifies key zoonotic viruses from Flaviviridae, Bunyaviridae, and Coronaviridae families circulating in rodents and insectivores, highlighting the role of small mammals as both reservoirs and vector feeders.
analysis.contribution: The study underscores the urgent need for improved epidemiological monitoring and interdisciplinary risk assessment to address the expanding range of zoonotic diseases driven by climate change and ecosystem transformation.
analysis.limitations: The analysis is based solely on the abstract, which provides a general overview without specific quantitative data, sample sizes, or detailed methodological descriptions.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Small mammals are key reservoirs for zoonotic viruses, causing significant public health concerns in Russia and globally. Methods: This review synthesizes data on viral pathogen circulation in small mammal populations in natural foci, focusing on surveillance and host-pathogen-vector dynamics. Results: It highlights the prevalence of Flaviviridae, Bunyaviridae, and Coronaviridae viruses in rodents and insectivores, noting their dual role as reservoirs and vector feeders. Contribution: The paper emphasizes the critical need for enhanced epidemiological monitoring and interdisciplinary approaches to manage expanding zoonotic disease risks. Limitations: The summary is derived exclusively from the abstract, lacking detailed quantitative results or specific methodological details.

papers.title_zh: 小型哺乳动物种群中循环的动物源性病毒病原体:现状概览

analysis_zh.background: 小型哺乳动物是人畜共患病毒的主要宿主,在俄罗斯联邦及全球构成显著的流行病学风险,每年记录数百例重症病例。
analysis_zh.methods: 本综述汇总了俄罗斯联邦及全球自然疫源区小型哺乳动物群体中病毒性人畜共患病原循环的最新数据,重点关注流行病学监测以及宿主‐病原‐媒介关系。
analysis_zh.results: 综述确定了在啮齿动物和食虫动物中循环的关键人畜共患病毒,主要来自黄病毒科、布尼亚病毒科和冠状病毒科,强调小型哺乳动物既是病毒储存宿主,也是为媒介提供血餐的宿主。
analysis_zh.contribution: 研究强调迫切需要加强流行病学监测和跨学科风险评估,以应对气候变化和生态系统转型推动的人畜共患疾病范围扩大的挑战。
analysis_zh.limitations: 本分析仅基于摘要,提供总体概述,缺乏具体定量数据、样本量或详细方法描述。

papers.title: The Potential Risk Factors of Hantavirus Transmission to Humans from Infected Rodents in Malaysia
papers.abstract: Zoonotic hantavirus is a negative single-stranded RNA virus from the family Bunyaviridae which is known to cause two significant rodent-borne diseases in humans namely hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), affecting about 30 000 people worldwide each year. HFRS is a disease found endemically in Asia and Europe with case fatality rates varying from <1% to 12%, while HPS which has a higher mortality rate of approximately 40% occurs within the American continent. Many countries in Southeast Asia unaware the public health implication of Hantavirus infection despite favorable ecological conditions include rich rodent species diversity, urbanisation and high human-wildlife interface that serve as ecological condition that could support the virus persistence and transmission.Since humans serve as spillover hosts who are infected largely by inhalation of infected rodents’ excreta, it is crucial to fill in the research gap by identifying the risk factors for human hantavirus infection. This paper provides a review of the potential risk factors associated with hantavirus transmission to humans from infected rodents in Malaysia focusing on behavioral, occupational, urban, and environmental. Other pieces of knowledge such as hantavirus virological properties, the geographical distribution with its respective role as a reservoir, clinical features, and diagnostic challenges, particularly its propensity to be misclassified due to mimic symptom with dengue and leptospirosis. To effectively mitigate transmission, Malaysia must transition from a fragmented surveillance model to a proactive, integrated One Health framework that bridges the inter-governmental agencies through a unified data-sharing platform to monitor active viral strains and prevent localised spillover outbreaks.
papers.journal: Pertanika Journal of Veterinary Medicine and Science

papers.title: Differential PCDH1 usage by Laguna Negra and Black Creek Canal hantaviruses
papers.abstract: Laguna Negra virus and Black Creek Canal virus are hantaviruses associated with hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), but their cellular entry receptors have not been defined. We used replication-competent recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses (rVSVs) bearing hantavirus Gn/Gc glycoprotein complexes to compare entry by these viruses, the Old World rodent-borne Dabieshan virus and Tigray virus, and the shrew-borne Cao Bang virus and Amga virus. All six Gn/Gc complexes supported infection of primary human pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells, with virus-specific efficiencies and kinetics. Genetic ablation of protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) reduced infection mediated by Laguna Negra virus and Black Creek Canal virus Gn/Gc in human osteosarcoma and endothelial cells, whereas PCDH1 re-expression restored susceptibility. Both viruses were captured by a soluble PCDH1 protein comprising the first two extracellular cadherin domains. Infection was also inhibited by a soluble decoy containing the first cadherin domain, and by an antibody specific to that domain, indicating that the first PCDH1 cadherin domain mediates viral engagement. Black Creek Canal Gn/Gc-bearing rVSVs incorporated less Gn/Gc and showed lower apparent capture by PCDH1 than Laguna Negra virus and Andes virus Gn/Gc-bearing particles, even after normalization for glycoprotein abundance. In contrast, PCDH1 depletion did not detectably alter infection mediated by the other four hantavirus Gn/Gc complexes. Thus, Laguna Negra virus and Black Creek Canal virus use PCDH1 for efficient entry but differ in apparent receptor engagement and responses to PCDH1-directed inhibitors, whereas all six viruses are potently neutralized by the broadly reactive Gn/Gc-directed antibody ADI-42898. Importance The receptors used by many medically important hantaviruses remain incompletely characterized. Using BSL2-compatible rVSVs bearing hantavirus glycoproteins, we show that Laguna Negra virus and Black Creek Canal virus, two hantaviruses associated with human cardiopulmonary disease, used protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) for efficient entry into human cells. PCDH1-directed inhibitors blocked infection, but the two viruses differed in apparent receptor engagement and inhibitor sensitivity, showing that PCDH1 usage is not uniform even among closely related viruses. Gn/Gc complexes from four additional divergent hantaviruses carried by shrews and Old World rodents infected primary human endothelial cells without detectable PCDH1 dependence, emphasizing the need to identify alternative entry factors. A broadly reactive antibody neutralized every virus in the study panel, supporting conserved viral glycoprotein surfaces as therapeutic targets when receptor usage is diverse or unknown.

Genetic ablation of protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) reduced infection mediated by Laguna Negra virus and Black Creek Canal virus Gn/Gc in human osteosarcoma and endothelial cells, whereas PCDH1 re-expression restored susceptibility. Both viruses were captured by a soluble PCDH1 protein comprising the first two extracellular cadherin domains. Infection was also inhibited by a soluble decoy containing the first cadherin domain, and by an antibody specific to that domain, indicating that the first PCDH1 cadherin domain mediates viral engagement. Black Creek Canal Gn/Gc-bearing rVSVs incorporated less Gn/Gc and showed lower apparent capture by PCDH1 than Laguna Negra virus and Andes virus Gn/Gc-bearing particles, even after normalization for glycoprotein abundance. In contrast, PCDH1 depletion did not detectably alter infection mediated by the other four hantavirus Gn/Gc complexes. Thus, Laguna Negra virus and Black Creek Canal virus use PCDH1 for efficient entry but differ in apparent receptor engagement and responses to PCDH1-directed inhibitors, whereas all six viruses are potently neutralized by the broadly reactive Gn/Gc-directed antibody ADI-42898. Importance The receptors used by many medically important hantaviruses remain incompletely characterized. Using BSL2-compatible rVSVs bearing hantavirus glycoproteins, we show that Laguna Negra virus and Black Creek Canal virus, two hantaviruses associated with human cardiopulmonary disease, used protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) for efficient entry into human cells. PCDH1-directed inhibitors blocked infection, but the two viruses differed in apparent receptor engagement and inhibitor sensitivity, showing that PCDH1 usage is not uniform even among closely related viruses. Gn/Gc complexes from four additional divergent hantaviruses carried by shrews and Old World rodents infected primary human endothelial cells without detectable PCDH1 dependence, emphasizing the need to identify alternative entry factors. A broadly reactive antibody neutralized every virus in the study panel, supporting conserved viral glycoprotein surfaces as therapeutic targets when receptor usage is diverse or unknown.

analysis.background: Laguna Negra virus and Black Creek Canal virus are hantaviruses linked to hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, but their cellular entry receptors were previously undefined (A1).
analysis.methods: Replication‑competent recombinant VSVs bearing each hantavirus Gn/Gc were used to assess entry into primary human pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells and other cell lines; PCDH1 was genetically ablated and re‑expressed, and soluble PCDH1 decoys and domain‑specific antibodies were employed (A2).
analysis.results: All six Gn/Gc complexes mediated infection of human endothelial cells with virus‑specific efficiencies (A3); PCDH1 knockout reduced infection by Laguna Negra and Black Creek Canal viruses, which was rescued by PCDH1 re‑expression (A4); both viruses were captured by soluble PCDH1 and blocked by a decoy or domain‑specific antibody (A5‑A6); Black Creek Canal Gn/Gc incorporated less glycoprotein and showed lower capture by PCDH1 than Laguna Negra virus (A7); PCDH1 depletion did not affect the other four hantaviruses (A8); a broadly reactive Gn/Gc‑directed antibody neutralized all six viruses (A9).
analysis.contribution: The study defines PCDH1 as a functional entry receptor for two HCPS‑associated hantaviruses, reveals heterogeneity in receptor engagement, underscores the need to identify alternative receptors for other hantaviruses, and highlights a broadly neutralizing antibody as a potential therapeutic (A10‑A14).
analysis.limitations: Only abstract data are provided; detailed quantitative metrics, sample sizes, in vivo validation, and broader methodological details are not reported.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Laguna Negra and Black Creek Canal hantaviruses cause HCPS but lacked defined entry receptors (A1). Methods: Recombinant VSVs bearing hantavirus Gn/Gc were used to test entry into human endothelial cells, with PCDH1 knockout/re‑expression and soluble decoys/antibodies (A2). Results: All six Gn/Gc mediated infection; PCDH1 loss reduced entry of Laguna Negra and Black Creek Canal viruses, rescued by re‑expression, and both were blocked by soluble PCDH1 or domain‑specific antibody, while other hantaviruses were PCDH1‑independent; a broad Gn/Gc antibody neutralized all (A3‑A9). Contribution: Identifies PCDH1 as a receptor for two HCPS viruses, shows variability in receptor use, points to other entry factors, and supports a universal neutralizing antibody (A10‑A14). Limitations: Only abstract information is available; detailed data and in vivo relevance are not reported.

papers.title_zh: Laguna Negra 与 Black Creek Canal 病毒对 PCDH1 的差异性利用 汉坦病毒es

analysis_zh.background: Laguna Negra 病毒和 Black Creek Canal 病毒是与 汉坦病毒心肺综合征 相关的 汉坦病毒es,但其细胞进入受体此前尚未确定 (A1)。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用携带各自 汉坦病毒 Gn/Gc 的复制兼容重组 VSVs 评估其进入原代人肺微血管内皮细胞及其他细胞系;对 PCDH1 进行基因敲除并重新表达,同时使用可溶性 PCDH1 噬菌体和域特异性抗体 (A2)。
analysis_zh.results: 所有六种 Gn/Gc 复合物均以病毒特异性效率感染人类内皮细胞 (A3);PCDH1 基因敲除降低了 Laguna Negra 病毒和 Black Creek Canal 病毒的感染率,重新表达 PCDH1 可恢复感染 (A4);两种病毒均被可溶性 PCDH1 捕获,并可被噬菌体或域特异性抗体阻断 (A5–A6);Black Creek Canal Gn/Gc 融合的糖蛋白较少,且被 PCDH1 捕获的效率低于 Laguna Negra 病毒 (A7);PCDH1 降解未影响其余四种 汉坦病毒es (A8);一种广泛结合 Gn/Gc 的抗体可中和所有六种病毒 (A9)。
analysis_zh.contribution: 本研究确立了 PCDH1 作为两种 HCPS 相关 汉坦病毒es 的功能性进入受体,揭示了受体结合的异质性,强调了寻找其他 汉坦病毒es 替代受体的必要性,并突出了广谱中和抗体作为潜在治疗手段 (A10–A14)。
analysis_zh.limitations: 仅提供了摘要数据;未报告详细定量指标、样本量、体内验证及更广泛的方法细节。
